Award Construction Contract for the Citywide Leading Pedestrian Intervals (LPI) Project (CS22B). Environmental Considerations: The project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15301(c), which categorically exempts minor alterations to existing public streets, sidewalks, gutters, and similar facilities, including the replacement or reconstruction of existing structures and facilities. This exemption includes improvements, such as pedestrian crossings, and other similar alterations that do not create additional automobile lanes.
Implementation of LPI operations modifies operations at existing signalized intersections to provide pedestrian safety enhancements. LPI is also considered a Vehicle Miles Traveled (VMT) reduction measure because it provides pedestrian network improvements. The proposed improvements are minor alterations to existing infrastructure and meet the criteria for this exemption. Contact Person: Associate Traffic Engineer II Edgeworth

10A.
1) Public hearing to consider a timely-filed appeal (Case No. APPEAL-007599-2024) of the Planning Commission's approval of a density bonus, tentative map, design review permit, and coastal development permit authorizing the demolition of all onsite structures; the subdivision of seven existing parcels into 30 single-family lots, one private road lot, one park lot, one Homeowners' Association lot, and two best management practices (BMP) lots for stormwater collection; the construction of 30 new single-family homes (27 market-rate units and three very-low affordable units); the installation of associated landscape, utility, drainage, stormwater, and site improvements; and a temporary construction trailer located at 1220, 1230, 1234, and 1240 Melba Road, and 1180 and 1190 Island View Lane (APNs 259-180-09, -10, 16, and -33, 259-181-02, -03, and -04); and 2) Modification of the Public Road Standards to allow improvements to Melba Road shown as Option B in the project plans. Environmental Considerations: An Environmental Impact Report (EIR) was prepared to analyze the potential environmental effects of the project in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). The draft EIR was published for a 45-day public review period from April 12, 2024, to May 28, 2024. Comments received during the public review period and corresponding responses are included in the Final EIR (Attachment CC-5). No responses were received from Federal or State agencies. Responses were received from one organization (Melba Alliance for a Safe and Healthy Environment (MASHE); and 19 individuals (several of whom submitted multiple comment letters). Following close of the EIR public review period, one additional letter was received from an individual.
Through the analysis provided in the EIR, it was determined that the project would result in significant environmental impacts, for the categories identified below, unless mitigation measures are incorporated to reduce the environmental impacts to less than significant levels:
* Biological Resources
* Cultural Resources
* Geology and Soils
* Hazards/Hazardous Materials
* Noise
* Tribal Cultural Resources
The Planning Commission adopted Resolution No. PC 2024-21 to certify the Final EIR, make required Findings of Fact, and adopt the Mitigation, Monitoring and Reporting Program (MMRP). The project is required to comply with the mitigations identified in the EIR and the MMRP. Contact Person: Project Planner Dichoso
1) Deny the appeal and adopt draft City Council Resolution No. 2024-124 titled, "A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Encinitas, California Denying the Appeal Filed by Melba Alliance for a Safe and Healthy Environment of and Affirming the Planning Commission's Decision Certifying a Final Environmental Impact Report, Adopting the Findings of Fact, and Adopting the Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program, All in Accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA); and Approving a Density Bonus, Tentative Map, Design Review Permit, and Coastal Development Permit for the Demolition of All Onsite Structures; the Subdivision of Seven Existing Parcels into 30 Single-Family Lots, One Private Road Lot, One Park Lot, One Homeowners' Association Lot, and Two Best Management Practices (BMP) Lots for Stormwater Collection; the Construction of 30 New Single-Family Homes (27 Market-Rate Units and Three Very-Low Affordable Units); the Installation of Associated Landscape, Utility, Drainage, Stormwater, and Site Improvements for the Property Located at 1220, 1230, 1234, 1240 Melba Road, and 1180 and 1190 Island View Lane (CASE NOS. Public Hearing to consider a timely-filed appeal of the Development Services Director's approval of a time extension for the Clark Avenue Apartments project that approved a 199-unit residential development with associated site improvements. CASE NOS.: MULTI-007384-2024, EXT-007415-2024, CDPNF-007414-2024; LOCATION: 662, 672, & 682 Clark Avenue and 556 Union (APNs: 256-171-25). Environmental Considerations: The extension of time has been determined to be exempt from environmental review pursuant to California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines Section 15061 (b)(3). This section exempts projects where it can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that the activity in question may have a significant effect on the environment. The project was determined to be statutorily exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Government Code Sections 65583.2(h) and (i), which provide that if a housing development project is located on a site designated for "by right" approval, contains at least 20 percent of the units affordable to lower income households, and does not require a subdivision, the City may only require design review approval of the project, and design review approval shall not constitute a "project" under CEQA. The Clark Avenue Apartment project is statutorily exempt from CEQA in that it is located in the R-30 Overlay Zone, which is designated for "by right" approval by Encinitas Municipal Code Chapter 30.09 (Zoning Use Matrix Note 35), proposes that 40 of 199 units, exclusive of additional units provided by a density bonus, will be affordable to lower income households; and does not require a subdivision. There are no proposed changes to the project as originally approved. Contact Person: Senior Planner Bustamante

10D.
Relocation of Encinitas Fire Station #1 from 415 Second Street to a temporary fire station at the Pacific View Cultural Arts Center Property located at 608 Third Street. Environmental Considerations: The project proposes the temporary location of a fire support trailer and garage on a developed site. Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines Sections 15269(c), 15301(b), 150303(c),15303 (e) and 15303 (f), the project would be exempt from environmental review. The relocation of Fire Station #1 is necessary to address an emergency at the current
location due to seismic safety conditions of the existing building consistent with Section 15269(c) of the CEQA Guidelines. The project is consistent with Section 15301(b) because it is located on
a developed site with existing parking and utilities such as gas, sewer, water and electrical amenities. The project is also consistent with Section 150303(c) because the total floor area of
the two (2) temporary buildings is less than the maximum 10,000-square foot floor area allowed under the exemption. Section 15303(e) exempts accessory (appurtenant) structures such as a
garage. Section 15304(f) exempts minor trenching conducted to connect to existing underground offsite utilities and the surface would be restored. The project does not qualify as one of the
exceptions prescribed under Section 15300.2 of the CEQA Guidelines and no historic resources are affected by the proposed project. Contact Person: Fire Chief Gordon
1) Approve the Emergency Declaration for construction of a temporary Fire Station #1; 2) Approve the temporary relocation of Encinitas Fire Station #1 from its current location at 415 Second Street to a temporary facility at the Pacific View Cultural Arts Center property located at 608 Third Street and provide direction on the Northwest or Southeast site options; 3) Adopt Resolution No. 2024-130, titled "A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Encinitas, California, Amending the Fiscal Year 2024-25 Budget" to appropriate $1.9M to the Emergency Fire Station #1 Relocation (CF25A) Project; and 4) Authorize the City Manager or her designee, in coordination with the City Attorney, to execute Amendment No. 4 to the Agreement with Michael Baker International, in substantial form, to add $250,000 to the engineering design consultant agreement for a new not-to-exceed contract amount of $750,000.

Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
